name: ebola_public_health
remarks: Ebola Public Health Overlay Submodule
Encodes post-discharge public-health response for EVD survivors:
isolation care plan, contact tracing, ring vaccination (Zaire only),
21-day contact monitoring, and survivor follow-up.
Called only from the recovery path of ebola_clinical_course — all patients
who reach this module are survivors.
Key interventions encoded:
- Isolation care plan with airborne + contact precautions
- Mandatory public health notification
- Ring vaccination notification (Zaire species only):
ERVEBO (rVSV-ZEBOV-GP): WHO-recommended, single dose, high efficacy.
No licensed reactive vaccine for Sudan or Bundibugyo (2026).
- 21-day contact follow-up period (WHO/CDC: contacts monitored for 21 days
after last exposure — the maximum incubation period)
- Survivor care plan for post-Ebola syndrome and semen testing counseling
(WHO guidance: sexual transmission documented up to 15 months post-recovery;
semen testing starts at 3 months, continues to 2 consecutive negatives)
Attributes set:
ebola_contact_tracing_status : 'initiated' -> 'completed'
ebola_isolation_active       : true -> false
ebola_ring_vax_ordered       : true (Zaire only — documents notification to contacts)
SNOMED codes marked 'verify' need confirmation against current release.
Confirmed codes (used in existing Synthea modules or ANDV module):
734163000  Care plan (record artifact)
409524006  Airborne precautions (procedure)
409526008  Contact precautions (procedure)
225344000  Use of personal protective equipment (procedure)
416940007  Mandatory notification of disease (procedure)
References:
- WHO EVD fact sheet 2025; WHO IPC guidance for EVD
- CDC EVD public health strategy; CDC contact definition and monitoring
- Guinea ring-vaccination trial (Lancet 2017); SAGE/CDC ERVEBO recommendation
- WHO survivor guidance: sexual transmission and semen testing
Full IPC care plan: airborne + contact precautions + PPE.
Applies to HCWs and any household contacts during isolation period.
SNOMED 734163000: Care plan (record artifact) — confirmed in existing modules.
Mandatory notification to public health authorities per WHO/CDC guidance.
Triggers contact listing and ring vaccination logistics for Zaire species.
ERVEBO ring vaccination recommended only for Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks.
No licensed reactive vaccine for Sudan or Bundibugyo (WHO 2026).
This state records the notification/ordering of ring vaccination for contacts —
the patient themselves has already recovered; this documents the public-health action.
Documents that ring vaccination with ERVEBO was ordered/initiated for identified
contacts of this confirmed Zaire EVD case.
ERVEBO (rVSV-ZEBOV-GP): single-dose, WHO-recommended; SAGE endorsed 2020.
CVX 213: rVSV-ZEBOV-GP Ebola vaccine. Verify CVX code against current registry.
21-day monitoring period per WHO/CDC: contacts followed for 21 days after
last exposure (maximum incubation period for all Ebola species).
This is shorter than ANDV (42 days) — Ebola incubation max is 21 days.
Post-Ebola syndrome monitoring and survivor support.
WHO guidance: survivors may experience fatigue, musculoskeletal pain,
ocular disease, and neurologic symptoms for months after recovery.
Male survivors: sexual transmission documented up to 15 months post-recovery.
WHO recommends semen testing at 3 months, continuing to 2 negative results.
WHO recommends semen testing for male survivors starting at 3 months.
Modeled as a 3-month delay then a counseling/testing encounter.
Female survivors and children do not require semen testing.
WHO guidance: semen testing begins at 3 months post-recovery.
